question: Which version 1.3 fields can provide a conservative read-only gameplay-availability gate across frontend, modal, and human-turn transitions?

scope.boundary: The accepted API gate is a conservative single-player read predicate. It does not call guest code, classify multiplayer fallback behavior, or authorize mutations.

dependencies.use: key-2 state factory and AudioGameStartInit entry
proved guest-main-thread frame boundary for the default-off observer
accepted initial 0x78-byte owner construction and publication at the selected resolver input global
historical bounded exact-global reference inventory and unresolved lifetime, kept separate from the selected +0x10 producer question

currentEvidence.method: combined foreground read-only Ghidra function, reference, instruction, pointer, and bounded-string queries with narrow generated-code corroboration and a default-off transition observer
currentEvidence.qualification: Runtime coverage confirmed main menu, new-game gameplay, AI and human turns, modal save UI, return to menu, and a load path. Human-player mask zero remains intentionally unavailable because the title's fallback calls session code.

frontendLifecycle.result: The check requires a non-null root-plus-0x70 current-state pointer and state key 2 before producing the self-identifying ingame result. Runtime observed key 1 at the main menu and key 2 during both new-game and loaded gameplay.
frontendLifecycle.boundary: Key 2 establishes frontend gameplay lifecycle only; it does not establish a human turn or an unobstructed game interface.

frontendRootCurrentStateRead.result: FrontendInGameStateCheck loads the frontend-root pointer from 0x82FFD624 and reads its current-state pointer at offset 0x70.
frontendRootCurrentStateRead.boundary: The concrete frontend-root class and complete layout remain unresolved. Key 2 remains a frontend lifecycle state rather than a complete gameplay-availability gate.

frontendStateKeyRead.result: FrontendInGameStateCheck reads the state key at offset 0x4 from the current-state pointer obtained through frontend-root offset 0x70.
frontendStateKeyRead.boundary: The complete frontend-state layout remains unresolved. Key 2 establishes frontend lifecycle only, not human-turn or interface availability.

interfaceUpdateFieldReadQuery.result: The bounded depth-zero field-access query recovered no READ-classified access at interface-state offset 0x5.
interfaceUpdateFieldReadQuery.boundary: The configured function exposed only two scanned instructions, so this result does not establish that InterfaceUpdateDebugRead performs no interface-state field read.

resolverBoundary.result: The resolver returns -1 when the input pointer at offset 0x10 is null. Otherwise it passes that pointer as r3, loads its vptr at +0x0, calls the word at vtable +0x100, and loads word +0xC from the returned r3 pointer. There is no result-pointer null check before the +0xC read.

inputProduction.result: The selected CombatResolve call loads r3 from 0x8314EFE0. The accepted 0x78-byte owner constructor retains the incoming pointer in r31 and passes it to 0x82D8D430. That base initializer sets r30=0 at 0x82D8D458 and stores it to the same owner +0x10 at 0x82D8D4F0. The outer constructor restores r3=r31 at 0x82D8D654 before the publication store at 0x82E2E55C.
inputProduction.qualification: This proves the initial null store and selected call input, under valid allocation and normal native ABI returns. Retaining null through later calls requires their effects not to alias owner +0x10. The alternative publisher store at 0x82E2E56C uses current r29 and does not identify a nonnull object producer. Same-address sign-in/network catalog aliases do not establish runtime object or field-role equivalence. No original concrete owner or +0x10 object type is assigned.

dispatchReturnContract.qualification: The nonnull arm requires a readable input object, readable vptr and slot cell, executable target, ABI-normal return, and a returned pointer with readable +0xC. These are operand requirements, not evidence that a native-produced nonnull object reaches this dispatch. The target, result-object producer, stored word meaning and valid returned range remain unresolved.

boundedProducerSupport.method: Foreground read-only ghidra/DumpMemoryWords.java and ghidra/FindRawGlobalStoreCandidates.java, exact native-word interpretation, and narrow generated windows with label-anchored mnemonic mapping. A separate custom exact-reference query capped the exact-global inventory at 32 rows.

globalStoreCandidates.qualification: The eight-word same-block lis/D-form search covers only its declared syntactic store forms. Its four emitted words are repeated in the raw windows and add no distinct words. It is not a complete publisher or object-field writer inventory.

globalReferenceBoundary.result: No sampled reference owner was expanded. Truncation stops selection of a later nonnull +0x10 writer. The historical complete reference inventory in save-profile-owner-lifetime-boundary.json remains a separate closed read set; neither inventory establishes absence of field writers.

boundedProducerSupport.checks: All 273 words match image.json size and SHA-256. The 272 instruction words map to exact generated mnemonic windows; zero padding 0x82D8D544 is excluded from code claims. Independent native operand checks bind the caller global, constructor/base call and zero store. Native resolver control/memory execution returns -1 from that zero field without dispatch. A synthetic nonnull dispatch fixture checks receiver/vptr/slot/CTR/result-pointer operands with adverse volatile clobbers; it supplies no object-production evidence. Five mutations detect a wrong initialization offset, vptr offset, dispatch slot, CTR source and result-word offset. Finite readable memory, normal ABI returns and nonalias effects remain conditions.
boundedProducerSupport.qualification: The bounded read set contains six native-supported functions and eight generated entries. The incidental generated prologue fragments [0x82D990E0,0x82D990F0) and [0x82D98918,0x82D98934) support no claims. The native read set includes the unrelated 64-word 0x82D8CC28 prefix, which establishes no +0x10 object producer. No complete CombatResolve, publisher, unselected helper arm or runtime execution is claimed. The unknown required nonnull writer and truncated exact-global reference inventory close this read set before any vtable cell or target can be selected.

resolverBoundary.boundary: The required later writer of a nonnull owner +0x10 object, its installed vptr, matching +0x100 cell, concrete dispatch target and exact returned-object producer remain unresolved. Initial null construction cannot prove that the field stays null for its lifetime. A new exact nonnull writer edge must bind this selected input before target or +0xC result semantics can be assigned. Fallback meaning and multiplayer/network semantics remain unresolved.

turnOwner.result: When the human-player mask is nonzero, 0x82CD5A70 classifies a player by testing its bit. The bounded turn-selection path writes selected player IDs to 0x8312B8E8 and can replace a human selection with the local player ID. Runtime observed player 0 as human, players 1-5 as AI, and restoration to player 0.
turnOwner.unknownRule: Mask zero, active player outside 0-31, or an unreadable scalar makes turn ownership unknown and the read API unavailable.
turnOwner.boundary: The immediate API must not invoke the classifier's mask-zero session fallback. Multiplayer and network-player semantics remain unresolved.

interfaceAvailability.result: The title's own debug reader loads byte 0x5 from the object published through 0x8314F28C. Runtime save-menu transitions cleared the byte and closing the modal restored it.
interfaceAvailability.boundary: The byte is an interface-update gate, not a general scene-active or gameplay-lifecycle flag.

availabilityPredicate.readPolicy: Resolve every pointer and scalar afresh at the proved frame boundary using bounded reads. Cache no guest pointers between frames.
availabilityPredicate.result: The predicate was unavailable at the main menu, the first incomplete load frame, AI turns, and save-menu modals; it became available on a known human turn with the interface gate enabled.

newGameRun.result: Key 2, active player 0, mask 1, and interface enabled produced available. Active players 1-5 produced unavailable, player 0 restored available, the modal interface clear produced unavailable, and frontend key 1 kept the predicate unavailable after return to menu.

loadRun.result: The load transition first exposed key 2 with unknown player state, then exposed player 0 and became available on the next frame.

reducedRegressionRun.ownerObservation: The owner reported clean text after repeated save-menu transitions and return to the main menu.
reducedRegressionRun.result: The reduced observer used only the accepted scalar gates, made no register captures or guest writes, and completed the load/save-menu/menu path without the text corruption seen with the broader observer.

abRegression.failure: A broader observer that dynamically scanned rejected processor and scene owners and emitted high-frequency transitions correlated with severe text corruption after opening the save menu.
abRegression.control: The same binary and path remained clean with the cvar off. After removing the rejected scans and restoring the no-register hook contract, the cvar-on reduced observer remained clean.
abRegression.qualification: The A/B test bounds the unsafe observer design but does not isolate one rejected read or log operation as the sole cause.

sceneActiveGate.result: The flag toggled transiently and remained true at the main menu, so it is not a gameplay lifecycle predicate.

gameInputProcessor.result: The registry object remained active during AI turns and does not classify the human-turn boundary.

gameStartByte.result: The byte is written during game start but no supported teardown clear was found.

driverOwner.result: The broad frame driver's owner is a rendering/update manager, not a gameplay-session identity.

importedInGameScreenRun.result: The imported name belongs to the Hall of Achievements owner and is not a gameplay lifecycle source.

guards: Resolve the frontend current-state and interface-gate pointers on every read; never retain them across frames or teardown.
Treat frontend key 2 as lifecycle only and require both a known human turn and interface update for availability.
When the human-player mask is zero, return unavailable instead of calling the title's session fallback from an immediate read API.
Do not use the scene-active gate, game-input registry, driver owner, or one-time game-start byte as availability inputs.
Do not reintroduce broad registry scans or high-frequency transition logging; repeat the save-menu/load/menu A/B regression after changing the observer.
The probe remains default-off, performs bounded reads only, and writes no guest memory or registers.
conclusion: For version 1.3, a conservative read-only gameplay API is available only when frontend state key 2 is current, the published interface object's update byte is enabled, and the active player is a known member of the nonzero human-player mask. The reduced default-off observer survived new game, AI/human turn changes, save-menu modal transitions, load, and return to menu without retaining guest pointers or reproducing the broader observer's text corruption.
